name: Neon
tagline: Serverless Postgres with branching, autoscaling, and an agent-ready API.
description: Neon's public API manages projects, branches, databases, and compute endpoints. The hosted MCP server exposes the same management surface over OAuth. API keys are Bearer tokens created in the console.

methods.label: API key
methods.note: Created in the console under Account settings → API keys; sent as a Bearer token.

methods.label: OAuth 2.0
methods.note: The hosted MCP server uses OAuth in supporting clients.

auth.guide:
**API key (REST):** create one under [Account settings → API keys](https://console.neon.tech/app/settings/api-keys) and send it as a Bearer token:

```bash
curl https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEON_API_KEY"
```

**MCP with OAuth (easiest):** add `https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp` in an OAuth-capable client and approve the consent screen.

Neon's published OpenAPI description also lists two cookie security schemes (`zenith`, `keycloak_token`). Those are the Neon console's own session cookies — not credentials you can create — so ignore them and use the Bearer key.

interfaces.name: Neon API
interfaces.note: The vendor spec declares the Neon console's session cookies (zenith, keycloak_token) as security schemes; the overrides remove them, leaving the real Bearer API-key auth.
